thread.title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point Higher Folllowing Upbeat Retail Sales, Empire State Index Data; Trump-Putin Summit in Focus

author: MT Newswires
title: ETF Preview: ETFs, Futures Point Higher Folllowing Upbeat Retail Sales, Empire State Index Data; Trump-Putin Summit in Focus
text:
Shutterstock photo Active broad-market exchange-traded funds ahead of Monday's regular session:
SPDR Select Sector Fund - Financial ( XLF ):+0.1%
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ): -0.03%
iShares MSCI Emerging Index Fund ( EEM ): -0.1%
iPath S&P 500 VIX ST Futures ETN ( VXX ): -0.3%
ProShares Trust Ultra VIX Short Term Futures ETF ( UVXY ): -0.2%
Broad Market Indicators
Broad-market exchange-traded funds, including IWM and IVV edged lower. Actively traded PowerShares QQQ (QQQ) was up 0.1%.
US stock futures were mostly higher ahead of Monday's open following reports that retail sales for June grew 0.5%, after a stronger-than-expected 0.8% increase in May. The ex-autos input rose 0.4% for the month from a better-than-expected 0.9% in the prior month.
Meanwhile, the Empire Manufacturing Survey for July climbed to 22.6 from the previous month's initial reading of 25.0.
Investors are also focusing on the meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
Looking ahead, the May reading for business inventories will be released at 10 am ET.
Power Play: Financial
The Select Financial Sector SPDRs ( XLF ) was up 0.1%. Direxion Daily Financial Bull 3X shares (FAS) was up 0.3% and its bearish counterpart Direxion Daily Financial Bear 3X shares (FAZ) was flat in pre-market trading .
Bank of America (BAC) rose 1.1% after the lender said Q2 EPS rose 43% to $0.63 from the year-ago period and topped the CapIQ mean for $0.57 normalized and $0.58 GAAP. Revenue, net of interest expense, decreased 1% to $22.6 billion but beat estimates for $22.49 billion.
Winners and Losers
Technology
Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) and other tech funds iShares Dow Jones US Technology ETF (IYW), iShares S&P North American Technology ETF (IGM) and iShares S&P North American Technology-Software Index (IGV) were inactive.
Among semiconductor ETFs, SPDR S&P Semiconductor (XSD) and Semiconductor Sector Index Fund (SOXX) were both flat.
Apple (AAPL) rose marginally after Bloomberg News, citing sources, said the company is dealing with the departure of key sales executives in India as the technology company grapples with low sales in the world's fastest-growing major smartphone market. The iPhone maker is taking the brunt from high tariffs on imported gadgets, causing consumers to flock to cheaper alternatives from Samsung and Xiaomi. The device maker resorts to marketing iPhones that are a few generations old and does not manufacture its latest models locally, thereby incurring import levies. Its inability to increase its single-digit market share is being blamed on Michel Coulomb, the country's head of operations, and his team which has been slow to cultivate business relationships domestically, sources said. His team has also failed to understand the Indian market, leaving the sales team aimless. Among the executives who have left the company are its national sales and distribution chief, the head of its commercial channels and mid-market business, and the head of telecom carrier sales, sources said. Representatives from Apple's India office did not respond to request for comments, Bloomberg News reported.
Energy
Dow Jones US Energy Fund (IYE) was flat while Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) was down 0.6%.
MDU Resources Group (MDU) said it has acquired the operations of Molalla Redi-Mix and Rock Products, a producer of ready-mix concrete in Molalla, Ore. MDU Resources anticipates the acquisition will be accretive to 2018 earnings per share. Additional financial details were not disclosed. Molalla Redi-Mix will become part of Knife River Corporation, the construction materials subsidiary of MDU. It will expand Knife River's reach into the market between Portland and Salem.
Commodities
Crude was down 2.2%. United States Oil Fund (USO) was down 1.4%. Natural gas was up 0.6% while United States Natural Gas Fund (UNG) was up 0.5%.
Gold was up 0.2%. SPDR Gold Trust (GLD) was up 0.1%. Silver was up 0.03%, while iShares Silver Trust (SLV) was down 0.2%.
Health Care
Health Care SPDR (XLV) was down 0.5% and other health care funds Vanguard Health Care ETF (VHT) and iShares Dow Jones US Healthcare (IYH) were flat. Biotechnology fund iShares NASDAQ Biotechnology Index (IBB) was flat in pre-market trading.
Tonix Pharmaceuticals Holding (TNXP) rose nearly 29%, and was on track to hit a new high since April 2017, after the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted fast track designation to its investigational new drug, TNX-102 SL, or Tonmya, to treat agitation in Alzheimer's disease. Tonmya is currently in a phase 3 study for military-related post-traumatic stress disorder, with an interim analysis expected in the Q3. The fast track designation is designed to facilitate the development and expedite the review of drugs to treat serious conditions and fill an unmet medical need. The benefits include rolling submission of portions of the new drug application (NDA) for the drug candidate, and eligibility for priority review of the NDA.
Consumer
Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR (XLP) and other funds Vanguard Consumer Staples ETF (VDC) and iShares Dow Jones US Consumer Goods (IYK) were flat.
Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR (XLY) rose 0.1% while retail funds SPDR S&P Retail (XRT), PowerShares Dynamic Retail (PMR) and Market Vectors Retail ETF (RTH) were inactive in pre-market territory.
Papa John's (PZZA) continued to deal with the fallout from the controversial remarks made by its resigned-chairman, John Schnatter, as professional and collegiate sports teams ended their relationship with the pizza restaurant chain, media reported. Schnatter resigned on Thursday after he admitted making a racist comment during a media training session. He also spoke in graphic terms about the lynching of African Americans in Indiana, where he spent his formative years. Shares fell some 1% in the pre-market session.
